findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A)  Inspectors observed multiple food items including but not limited to chicken, beans, and pork in stainless steel food containers stored in the walk-in cooler and the stainless steel double doors standing cooler in the kitchen. Inspectors also saw a container of chicken that was dated12/25/25 but the used by date had expired. PIC told inspectors that the food items were made the day before. PIC discarded the container of chicken dated 12/25/25 as a corrective action. PIC also instructed a staff member to properly date the food items that were not properly dated marked. Ensure that food items that are prepared and being stored for more than 24-hours are properly date marked and stored. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee was washing their while hands wearing gloves. The employee was informed that gloves are single-use and cannot be washed. They removed their gloves and went to grab new gloves. The inspector informed the employee that they must wash their hands before donning gloves. The inspector proceeded to demonstrate the proper hand washing procedure for the employees in the kitchen and the PIC translated. Ensure that all employees always used the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed there were two coolers for cold holding foods at 14F or below during the inspection:

(1) The standing refrigerator was observed to malfunction distorting the temperature of various food items stored it. The following food items were discarded due to the refrigerator malfunction.
1. Cheese dips (9 containers) = 49-51F
2. Salsa = 49F
3. carnitas = 52F
4. Tamale =49.2F
5. Sheers cake (2 Containers)= 51F
6. Stuffed peppers = 48.7F
Discussed with PIC that the above items were to be discarded because they had been prepared 3/07/25 and place in the refrigerator from the preparation date. Four containers of beans were observed to have internal temperatures between 39-42F and were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. Ensure that equipments are routinely checked for temperature observation to avoid food spoilage.

(2) The prep cooler at the bar was not cold holding foods above 41F. The following temperatures were reordered:
1. Diced tomatoes 51F
2. Sour scream 55F
3. Guac 55F
The temperature-control for safety (TCS) foods inside the cooler (diced tomatoes, pico, sour cream, cheese, and ranch) were discarded during the inspection. The mango hot sauce was non-TCS and allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC will be using ice baths to keep TCS items inside the cooler below 41F or under. The PIC was instructed to check the temperature regularly to ensure that the ice baths are sufficient for cold holding. The PIC will be using ice baths until the cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.

 The PIC called and scheduled maintenance for tomorrow. The inspector will follow-up to check on the temperatures for both coolers on 3/14/2025. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There was observed a pan of chicken int he double door cooler in the kitchen with a date of 6/25. This item was pulled from service and discarded during today’s inspection due to being past the 7 day rule. Ensure that all food items are checked and either used or discarded on the 7th day after prep. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Taco shells were discarded and moved as neccessary. 2) Observed the ice bin in the waitress station to be stored in the open position when not in use. Ice bin was pulled closed. 3) Observed an open can of tomato sauce in the reach in cooler in the kitchen. Acidic foods such as this must be transfered to a food grade container after opening the can.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed an employee wiping gloved hands that had just handled raw animal products on two towels that were hanging from his waist. He then used those towels as hot pads to handle plates. Avoid the use of common towels--if hands need to be wiped, they most likely need to be washed. Wiping cloths used for raw animal products should be used for no other purpose and stored in sanitizer solution in between use. Towels were removed.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment: Foods are still on steam table that were there during the fire. Discard all open, uncovered foods in the kitchen including the foods that are present on the steam table which is adjacent to the location of the fire. 3-101.11  (P) All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. Reference 3-101.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Wash, rinse, and sanitize all dishes, pans, cutting boards and other food contact surfaces in the kitchen that were exposed at the time of the fire.  4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Discard open single service items in kitchen at the time of the fire. Single service items in the process of being discarded. 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Hood system, baffles, walls, and ceiling in the kitchen where the fire occurred need to be cleaned from visible soot. Wipe down all containers if they are not able to be run through the dish machine. This is in process. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee remove gloves upon request and then was hands with soap very briefly before rinsing and turning the faucet off with bare hands. Hands must be scrubbed with soap for at least 10-15 seconds, rinsed and then a barrier should be used to turn faucet off so as to not re-contaminate hands. Hand washing was discussed at the time of the inspection. 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Dish machine tested at 0 ppm on the first run during the inspection. Bucket of sanitizer was changed out and primed and tested at 100 ppm to correct the violation. 4-501.114  (P) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Ice bins in the facility were stored in the open position when not in use. Keep ice bins closed when not in use. 3-305.11  (C)  Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed in use knives stored in the space between the oven and the prep cooler. This space is not easily cleanable. Store knives in an area that is clean and sanitized, and wash, rinse and sanitize in use utensils at least every 4 hours. 3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.comment: Observed employee use gloved hands to place raw chicken on the grill, briefly wash/rinse hands with the same gloves on and attempt to return to food preparation. Employee was stopped and proper glove use and hand washing discussed. 3-304.15 (A) P Single use gloves shall be used for only one task and discarded.
